dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: AL amyloidosis (primary systemic light-chain amyloidosis) presenting with spontaneous bilateral periorbital purpura, due to amyloid deposition weakening the periorbital dermal blood vessels

1. Acquired or occult bleeding disorder (e.g., acquired von Willebrand disease, mild platelet function defect) not detected on initial screening
2. Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis with periorbital predilection
3. Repeated occult Valsalva (forceful coughing/sneezing/straining) causing periorbital purpura in the setting of an unrecognised capillary fragility disorder
order_raw:
1. Valsalva manoeuvre to assess for provocation of periorbital purpura
2. Tourniquet test (Rumpel-Leede) to assess capillary fragility
3. Full blood count with differential and platelet count
4. Coagulation studies (PT, aPTT, fibrinogen)
5. Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation
6. Serum free light chain assay
7. 24-hour urine collection for total protein and light chain electrophoresis
8. Punch biopsy of the periorbital skin with Congo red staining for amyloid
9. MRI of the brain and orbits with gadolinium contrast
10. Formal ophthalmology assessment with visual acuity, visual field testing, slit-lamp, and dilated fundoscopy
dx: AL amyloidosis (primary systemic light-chain amyloidosis) presenting with spontaneous bilateral periorbital purpura, due to amyloid deposition weakening the periorbital dermal blood vessels
